claim: herdr_env_ready tests `herdr_env >= "1"` (string order) where readHerdrEnvironment tests `=== "1"`, so with HERDR_ENV="2" (or any value sorting at or after "1" byte-wise: "10", "1 ", "1\n", "true", "yes", "w1:p7", ...) and both other variables non-empty, herdr_env_ready is true while readHerdrEnvironment returns null.
notes: Seen on reading types.ail:1433, confirmed on the real functions: 227 of 344 cases in the HERDR_ENV slice (every string of length <=2 over 18 chars around "1"), 14,728 of 42,524 in the full sweep, 42,474 and 42,757 of 200,000 random cases (seeds 1, 2). AILANG is the side that departs from the documented rule (HERDR_ENV=1, herdr-agent-state.ts:158). The 5 inline tests pass: besides "1" they try HERDR_ENV only as "" and "0", both below "1". Control: mutants.sh fix-ail-env (`>=` -> `==`) turns this repro to 0 and leaves the others at 1. Reachability: herdr itself injects "1"; another value needs an operator or wrapper to set e.g. HERDR_ENV=true in a pane. The extension then advertises Delegate/DelegateCheck and drives herdr while the TUI stays invisible to it. Also fires end to end through buildChildEnv and register_with_config (X-2 sweep, HERDR_ENV in {"2","true","w1:p7"}).

claim: readHerdrEnvironment rejects the binary only when HERDR_BIN_PATH is undefined (`bin === undefined`, herdr-agent-state.ts:164), so with HERDR_BIN_PATH set to "" it returns {paneId, bin: ""} while herdr_env_ready returns false.
notes: Seen on reading, confirmed on the real functions: the only mismatch in the HERDR_BIN_PATH slice (1 of 114), 186 of 42,524 in the full sweep, 1,684 and 1,697 of 200,000 random cases. The TS side departs from its own comment ("a pane id with no binary cannot report", :159) and from its paneId check, which uses `!paneId`. The TS tests try HERDR_PANE_ID="" but not HERDR_BIN_PATH="". Effect: initHerdrReporter goes active and every report spawns "" (ENOENT, swallowed). Control: mutants.sh fix-ts-bin (`!bin`) turns this repro to 0. Through the real pipeline the two sides happen to agree here, because buildChildEnv drops the empty value and register.ail then substitutes "herdr" (A1-T1-3).

claim: register_with_config, the only caller of herdr_env_ready, reads `getEnvOr("HERDR_BIN_PATH", "herdr")` (register.ail:49), so with HERDR_BIN_PATH unset (HERDR_ENV=1, HERDR_PANE_ID set) the extension advertises Delegate and DelegateCheck while readHerdrEnvironment returns null for the same environment.
notes: P1.1 assumes unset reaches herdr_env_ready as "", but at its only call site unset becomes "herdr". That makes the inline test (("1", "", "w1:p7"), false) unreachable from a real environment, and it contradicts types.ail:1290 ("if it is unset this extension should not have registered at all"), types.ail:1407 ("ALL THREE ARE REQUIRED") and the reason for HERDR_BIN_PATH at types.ail:1417 and register.ail:46: the extension then runs `herdr` from PATH. Executed on the real register_with_config in a real ailang process: 6 such environments in the X-1 sweep of 512, and 5 in the X-2 sweep through the real buildChildEnv (HERDR_PANE_ID=" " is dropped there, see A1-T1-4). verify_herdr_gate (Makefile:2744) tries only all-unset and all-set. Control: mutants.sh fix-register-bin (default "") turns this repro to 0.

claim: With HERDR_PANE_ID=" " (whitespace only), HERDR_ENV=1 and a binary, readHerdrEnvironment is non-null, but buildChildEnv forwards a HERDR_* variable only when `value.trim() !== ""` (runtime-process.ts:631), so the runtime child sees no pane id and the extension advertises no tools: the two copies disagree end to end although each function accepts " ".
notes: Outside both functions: the forwarding filter that herdr-agent-state.ts:152-155 names as "what stands between the two copies". P1.1 holds on this input; the disagreement comes from the filter. 7 such environments in the X-2 sweep of 512 (HERDR_ENV=1, HERDR_PANE_ID=" ", HERDR_BIN_PATH set). Low reachability: herdr injects real pane ids. The same filter turns HERDR_BIN_PATH="" or " " into unset, which then meets A1-T1-3. Controls: forwarding set values verbatim (mutants.sh fix-forward-verbatim) turns this repro to 0 and keeps P1.1 clean. Trimming in the TS twin alone (fix-ts-pane-blank) also turns it to 0 but opens a P1.1 mismatch in the HERDR_PANE_ID slice, because only one copy moved.
